chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-01.proposition: Classical divine simplicity excludes multiple kinds of composition in God, including distinctions between essence and existence, attributes, action, potency, and matter.

orphanFallback.rationale: The move independently specifies the breadth of composition denied by classical divine simplicity and therefore supplies conceptual groundwork without requiring an opposing move.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-04.proposition: A part may be understood as any positive ontological item intrinsic to a subject but distinct from that subject, so absolute divine simplicity requires anything intrinsic to God to be identical to God.

orphanFallback.rationale: This definition independently fixes the composition criterion used by the con route to test alleged divine distinctions, regardless of whether an earlier opposing move is retained.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-07.proposition: Divine aseity need not entail simplicity because dependence may be merely counterfactual, the whole may ground its parts, Trinitarian multiplicity may resist the stronger demand, or aseity may exclude only external dependence.

orphanFallback.rationale: Even without the earlier aseity argument, the surveyed accounts positively establish alternative conceptions of divine independence under which intrinsic multiplicity does not compromise aseity.

chunk-002:c002-01.proposition: Trinitarianism and absolute divine simplicity form an inconsistent tetrad if eternal processions are positive ontological items intrinsic to God yet distinct from God.

orphanFallback.rationale: The inconsistent-tetrad formulation directly advances the con route by deriving a conflict from Trinitarian processions and the stated criterion of composition without presupposing a reply target.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: Because the Son is begotten while God as such is not begotten, the Son appears strictly distinct from the Godhead and, being intrinsic rather than extrinsic to God, constitutes composition under the stated part criterion.

orphanFallback.rationale: Absent the earlier identity account, the asymmetric predicates of being begotten and not begotten still provide a standalone argument for a real intrinsic distinction between the Son and the Godhead.

chunk-002:c002-05.proposition: If God freely creates nothing, no positive ontological item is extrinsic to God in that world, so God's knowledge of contingent truths would be a contingent intrinsic item incompatible with divine simplicity.

orphanFallback.rationale: The alone-world argument independently combines creative freedom, omniscience, and the absence of extrinsic reality to derive contingent intrinsic divine knowledge.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: If an immutable and purely actual God cannot gain or lose knowledge while omniscience of changing contingent reality requires such epistemic change, then classical theism cannot accommodate that changing reality.

orphanFallback.rationale: The act-potency objection is presented as an independent argument from divine immutability, omniscience, and changing truths, so its force does not depend on any retained opposing move.
